queries.title: The RACI barrier-channel rate is the Marcus two-parabola rate
queries.chemicalQuestion: At the same pre-exponential factor and with beta = 1/(k_B T), is the RACI nonradiative barrier-channel rate A·exp(-beta·B), evaluated at the Marcus barrier B = (lam - x)^2/(4 lam), the Marcus rate A·exp(-DeltaGddagger/(k_B T)) of the same step?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both theories describe one barrier-controlled step. Marcus writes the rate as A·exp(-barrier(lam,x)/(k_B T)) with barrier = (lam - x)^2/(4 lam); RACI writes the conical-intersection channel as A·exp(-beta·B), with B the barrier that the accessibility constraint imposes on the torsion coordinate. Substituting the Marcus barrier and beta = 1/(k_B T) makes the two rate laws the same real function of the driving force, so the RACI CI channel is the Marcus step written with the transfer rate barrier. The query is a rate-law identification only; it does not identify the Marcus solvent coordinate with the RACI torsion angle, and the legacy look-alike row on the different crossing objects remains true.

queries.title: Is the torsion-blocked RACI crossing the Hammond transition-state coordinate?
queries.chemicalQuestion: The RACI constraint |theta| >= delta removes a neighbourhood of the conical point theta = 0 and the nonradiative rate drops through the barrier 2·delta; in Hammond's two-parabola description the crossing position tsCoord(lam,x) = (lam - x)/(2 lam) moves towards the product side as the driving force increases. Is the RACI accessibility gap the Hammond reactant/product-side displacement, i.e. does blocking the torsion coordinate correspond to a late (product-like) transition state?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both theories locate a crossing between two surfaces: Hammond by the transition-state coordinate tsCoord in (0,1) of a two-parabola step, RACI by the torsion angle theta whose zero is the conical intersection; both make a barrier a function of the crossing position. The chemical question is whether the RACI geometric blocking is the Hammond statement that the crossing has moved to the product side, which would identify the two "distance from the crossing" quantities. The corpus delivers no such identification: RACI never mentions a two-parabola coordinate and Hammond never mentions a torsion angle or a conical intersection, and the two barrier families differ (2·delta versus (lam - x)^2/(4 lam)).

queries.title: Is the BEP activation energy the RACI conical-intersection barrier?
queries.chemicalQuestion: The delivered BEP bridge rate_eq_exp_neg_eact states that the Marcus rate of a step equals A·exp(-eact(lam, x)/(k_B T)); the RACI barrier channel is A·exp(-beta·B). Is the BEP activation energy eact(lam, x) the barrier B of the RACI conical-intersection channel, so that the RACI rate at the BEP barrier is the BEP rate law of the same step?
queries.chemicalRationale: BEP's content is the activation energy eact(lam, x) and its linear-response behaviour; RACI's barrier B is the minimal accessible gap to the conical intersection, raised by the torsion constraint. Both feed an Arrhenius exponential, and the delivered BEP bridge theorem makes the algebraic substitution immediate. The chemical question is whether the reactive activation energy of a bond-making/bond-breaking step and the CI accessibility gap of a unimolecular nonradiative channel are the same physical barrier. Nothing in the corpus says they are: BEP has no electronic-state model and RACI has no reaction-energy surface, and the legacy register explicitly records no shared scalar. Certifying the exponential substitution would therefore assert a relation from algebraic shape alone, which the R1 boundary forbids; the honest outcome is to keep the candidate open.

queries.title: The RACI emission yield is the Kasha radiative branching probability
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the RACI two-channel yield kr/(kr + knr), evaluated at kr = rad n and knr = ic n, the Kasha radiative branching probability rad n/(rad n + ic n) of the same ladder level?
queries.chemicalRationale: Kasha assigns each ladder level n a radiative rate rad n and an internal-conversion rate ic n; the radiative branch radBranch is the probability that the level emits a photon. RACI writes the same two-channel competition as kr/(kr + knr). After unfolding the two definitions the two terms are the same term, so the relation is definitional: the RACI emission yield is the Kasha radiative branch of the emitting level, not a parallel definition. The equality carries no positivity premise because both yields are totalized divisions.

queries.title: Is the Sabatier volcano activity the RACI barrier channel?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Sabatier writes the catalytic activity as the Arrhenius exponential activity f kB T dE = exp(-(f dE)/(k_B T)) of a volcano barrier; RACI writes the nonradiative channel as A·exp(-beta·B). At A = 1 and beta = 1/(k_B T), is the Sabatier activity the RACI barrier channel at B = volcanoBarrier(dE)?
queries.chemicalRationale: The two theories share the Arrhenius functional form: a rate or activity that is the exponential of a barrier over k_B T. The chemical question is whether the Sabatier volcano activity and the RACI nonradiative channel are the same physical observable in a shared context, i.e. whether a catalytic adsorption-energy barrier is the conical-intersection accessibility barrier. The corpus gives no statement connecting the two barrier arguments: Sabatier has no electronic state, no conical intersection and no photophysical yield, and RACI has no adsorption energy and no catalytic descriptor. The shared exponential shape is precisely the "algebraic shape alone" that the R1 boundary forbids admitting as a relation, so the candidate is recorded as open.

queries.title: Is any Goldschmidt statement in the RACI jurisdiction?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is there a shared context or a declared translation between Goldschmidt's tolerance-factor and substitution predicates over ionic radii and the RACI conical-intersection kinetics?
queries.chemicalRationale: Goldschmidt's statements are geometric predicates on ionic radii: the tolerance factor (rA + rO)/(sqrt 2·(rB + rO)), the tolerance band, the A-site radius interval, and a substitution radius match. RACI's statements are a 2x2 electronic Hamiltonian, the torsion angle, an accessibility gap, an Arrhenius nonradiative rate and a two-channel yield. A named query needs two inventory statements, a shared context and translations into both statement contexts. No Goldschmidt statement mentions an electronic state, an energy gap, a rate or a yield, and no RACI statement mentions an ionic radius, a lattice geometry or a tolerance factor. The jurisdiction reason is therefore statement-level and chemical, not the cluster label: Goldschmidt's observables are lattice-geometry predicates and RACI's are excited-state kinetics, so there is no shared measured quantity to compare.

queries.title: Is the RACI conical point the beta = 1/2 symmetry-factor crossing?
queries.chemicalQuestion: The RACI torsion Hamiltonian has its conical intersection exactly at theta = 0 (torsionH_conicalSet) with the gap 2|theta| about it; the SymmetryFactor equal-curvature thermoneutral crossing sits at the beta = 1/2 coordinate tsCoordZero(kr, kp), and the accepted R3 tie-back identifies that coordinate with the kernel coordinate. Is the RACI conical point the same crossing as the SymmetryFactor beta = 1/2 crossing, i.e. are the two crossing coordinates the same physical coordinate?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both are two-surface crossing statements: one degeneracy of a 2x2 electronic Hamiltonian in a torsion angle, one crossing of two equal-curvature parabolas in a normalized reaction coordinate. The Marcus/SymmetryFactor R3 row certified its tie-back through the kernel barrier, but RACI has no kernel entry point: its conical set is a degeneracy of the matrix entries (a = d, b = 0), not a height of the kernel barrier. A relation would need a delivered identification of the torsion angle with the normalized crossing coordinate and of the matrix degeneracy with the surface crossing; neither exists in the corpus, so the crossing-coordinate equality is a candidate, not a certificate.

queries.title: Is any KashaVavilov statement a barrier, CI or CI-limited-yield statement?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Does any delivered KashaVavilov statement relate its spectral-invariance ladder (SpecSame, the Vavilov criterion) to the RACI yield or conical-intersection observables, so that a named statement-level query could be certified?
queries.chemicalRationale: KashaVavilov is the spectral side of the Kasha ladder: it states when the emission spectrum is independent of the excitation level (SpecSame) and separates Kasha from Vavilov behaviour. RACI is the kinetic/CI side: barriers, accessibility, nonradiative rate, yield. A relation would need a KashaVavilov statement mentioning a barrier, a conical intersection, or a CI-limited nonradiative rate, or a RACI statement mentioning a spectrum; a scoped search over the 29 KashaVavilov statements and the 71 RACI statements found none. The only KashaVavilov yield row, fluoYield_eq_emitYield_zero_add_upperYield, is Kasha's yield algebra, whose RACI relation is already the P-Kasha-RACI query Q-CI-KS-01; re-screening it here would double-count one relation under two pair labels.

queries.title: Dynamic quenching dilutes the RACI yield by the Stern-Volmer ratio
queries.chemicalQuestion: When a collisional quencher adds the channel kq·[Q] to the RACI nonradiative rate, is the quenched RACI yield Phi(kr, knr + kq·[Q]) equal to the unquenched yield divided by the Stern-Volmer intensity ratio (k0 + kq·[Q])/k0, with k0 = kr + knr?
queries.chemicalRationale: Stern-Volmer models dynamic quenching as an extra concentration-dependent decay channel kq·[Q] on top of the intrinsic total k0, and reports the intensity ratio (k0 + kq·[Q])/k0. RACI models its nonradiative loss as the barrier-controlled CI channel. If the quencher acts as an added nonradiative channel, the RACI yield must be diluted by exactly the SV ratio; the query asks whether that composition holds, i.e. whether an external collisional channel and the barrier-controlled CI channel combine in the RACI yield the way the SV ratio predicts. The two mechanisms run in opposite directions (SV adds an escape channel, RACI removes one), so the query composes them instead of identifying them.

queries.title: The RACI yield aggregates the FluorPhos S1 nonradiative channels
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the RACI two-channel yield at kr = kF and knr = kISC + kIC the FluorPhos S1 fluorescence yield kF/(kF + kISC + kIC)?
queries.chemicalRationale: FluorPhos resolves the S1 nonradiative decay into intersystem crossing and internal conversion and reports the fluorescence yield as the radiative share of the three-channel total. RACI has a single nonradiative channel. Identifying the RACI knr with the sum kISC + kIC turns the RACI yield into the FluorPhos S1 fluorescence yield, which is the chemical content of the RACI single-sink idealisation: the CI-mediated internal conversion and the intersystem crossing are summed as parallel nonradiative losses of the same S1 population. The query does not claim that the RACI CI channel and the FluorPhos ISC channel are the same mechanism; it claims that the yield of the summed three-channel decay is the RACI two-channel yield at the aggregated knr.

queries.title: The gap-law nonradiative rate is the RACI barrier channel at the gap barrier
queries.chemicalQuestion: At beta = 1/(k_B T) and B = nrBarrier(lam, x), is the RACI barrier channel the EnergyGapLaw nonradiative rate A·exp(-nrBarrier(lam, x)/(k_B T))?
queries.chemicalRationale: EnergyGapLaw defines the nonradiative rate of the excited state through the crossing barrier (lam - x)^2/(4 lam) and rewrites its logarithm as the gap law. RACI defines the conical-intersection channel as the same Arrhenius exponential with the CI accessibility gap as the barrier. Substituting the gap-law barrier makes the two the same rate function, so the RACI CI channel is the gap-law nonradiative rate at the gap-law barrier. The query is about the rate; it does not import the gap-law inverted-region monotonicity, which is a statement about lnRate rather than about the CI accessibility constraint.

queries.title: Is the RACI torsion gap the Stokes-shifted emission gap?
queries.chemicalQuestion: StokesShift builds the ground and excited surfaces s0(q) = lam·q^2 and s1(q) = lam·(q - 1)^2 + e00 and reports the emission energy and the Stokes shift 2·lam at the relaxed excited geometry. The RACI torsion Hamiltonian has the gap 2|theta|, vanishing at the conical point. Is the RACI gap the StokesShift surface gap, i.e. is the torsion angle the StokesShift displacement coordinate?
queries.chemicalRationale: The two theories are both two-surface, one-coordinate models. The RACI gap is linear in the coordinate and vanishes at the conical point; the StokesShift surface gap s1 - s0 is linear in q and vanishes where the two surfaces cross. The shared observable would be the surface gap as a function of the coordinate. But the corpus states no map q <-> theta, no identification of the emission-energy offset e00 with a torsion parameter, and the RACI gap is a degeneracy gap of a matrix while the StokesShift gap is an energy difference between two displaced parabolas; the legacy register records no edge precisely because the surface families differ. The shape coincidence alone is not a shared context.

sharedContext.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the StokesShift ground/excited surface gap s1(q) - s0(q) in the displacement coordinate q, compared with the RACI torsion gap 2|theta|. Both gaps are linear and vanish at a crossing, but no map q <-> theta is delivered.

queries.title: The internal-conversion rate is the RACI barrier channel at the FC barrier

queries.chemicalRationale: ICvsISC splits the nonradiative decay into internal conversion through a Franck-Condon barrier and intersystem crossing carrying a spin factor. RACI is the theory of the conical-intersection channel: its barrierRate is the nonradiative rate through the accessible conical intersection, and the legacy §17 row icvsisc_barrier_zero_at_crossing records that the two-parabola FC barrier vanishes at the crossing (the maximal-rate point). Identifying the barrier argument with the ICvsISC FC barrier makes the RACI CI channel exactly the ICvsISC internal-conversion rate. The intersystem-crossing channel stays outside the comparison because RACI has no spin observable.

queries.title: Is Forster transfer a competing RACI nonradiative channel?
queries.chemicalQuestion: If a donor with radiative rate kr and nonradiative rate knr acquires the Forster transfer channel kT, is the donor RACI yield Phi(kr, knr + kT) the unquenched yield multiplied by one minus the Forster transfer efficiency E = kT/(kD + kT) with kD = kr + knr, i.e. is the FRET channel an extra nonradiative channel in the RACI yield calculus?
queries.chemicalRationale: Forster transfer adds a distance-dependent decay channel to the donor excited state and reports the transfer efficiency E = kT/(kD + kT), equivalently 1 - tauDA/tauD (the delivered fretEff_via_lifetime row). RACI's yield is a two-channel competition. If the transfer channel is an added nonradiative channel, the donor yield must fall to (1 - E)·Phi0, which would make the FRET channel a conditional composition of the two calculi. The composition needs delivered bridges kD = 1/tauD and kT = fretRate tauD r6 R, plus a statement that the RACI knr is the donor intrinsic nonradiative rate; the corpus delivers none of these, and the legacy register records no shared scalar.

sharedContext.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: a donor with radiative kr and nonradiative knr plus a Forster transfer channel kT = fretRate tauD r6 R; the composition would need tauD = 1/(kr + knr) and kT = fretRate tauD r6 R as delivered premises, which the corpus does not state.
